title: Affine schemes have no positive quasi-coherent fppf cohomology
statement: Fix small presentations of sites in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $U$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $F$ be an arbitrary quasi-coherent Zariski $\mathcal O_U$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. On the big fppf site $\mathcal C_U=(\mathit{Sch}/U)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$ [def-pc-fppf-site], let $F^a$ be the associated module sheaf of [lem-sfb-scheme-big-fppf-quasicoherent-equivalence], with $F^a(v:T\to U)=\Gamma(T,v^*F)$ and tensor-pullback restrictions [def-pc-module-pullback]. Write $(F^a)_{ab}$ for its underlying abelian sheaf. Then $$H^q(\mathcal C_U,(F^a)_{ab})=0\qquad(q>0),$$ where $H^q$ is the right derived functor of evaluation at the terminal object $\operatorname{id}_U$ in abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-sp-injective-resolutions]. No finite-generation, flatness or Noetherian hypothesis on $F$ or $U$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 03DW (descent.tex, proposition-same-cohomology-quasi-coherent), part (1) with tau = fppf: H^q(U,F) = H^q((Sch/U)_fppf, F^a); combined with Tag 01XB (coherent.tex, lemma-quasi-coherent-affine-cohomology-zero) for affine U. Used in Tag 0DEW (etale-cohomology.tex, lemma-review-quasi-coherent), proof of (7), affine-cover paragraph, vanishing of H^p_fppf(U_i,F^a) for affine U_i. This is the affine intermediate conclusion, not the higher-direct-image assertion.

proof.text: Put $G=(F^a)_{ab}$ on $\mathcal C_U$. The associated-sheaf theorem gives precisely the sheaf with the section and restriction formulas in the statement. Let $\mathcal B$ be all objects $v:V\to U$ whose source is affine, and let $\mathrm{Cov}$ consist of all finite affine fppf covering families of members of $\mathcal B$. A finite iterated fibre product of affine schemes over an affine scheme is affine: repeatedly use the spectrum-of-tensor-product description, including repeated factors. Thus targets, members and all nonempty iterated fibre products of a covering in $\mathrm{Cov}$ lie in $\mathcal B$. This verifies hypothesis (1) of the general-site Cech criterion.

source.place: Tag 03DW, proposition-same-cohomology-quasi-coherent, proof, first affine-objects paragraph (using Tags 03F9 and 03FJ).

proof.text: For any $v:V\to U$ in $\mathcal B$ and any fppf covering $\{T_i\to V\}$, apply the affine-refinement theorem to its affine target $V$. It supplies a finite jointly covering family of affine opens $W_j\subseteq T_{i(j)}$, each flat and locally of finite presentation over $V$, with the displayed factorizations through $T_{i(j)}$. Composing their structure maps with $v$ makes this a covering in $\mathcal C_U$ refining the original covering. It belongs to $\mathrm{Cov}$, so hypothesis (2), cofinality at every affine object, holds.

source.place: Tag 021P, lemma-fppf-affine; the cofinality input to Tag 03DW.

proof.text: Apply the finite affine fppf Cech-vanishing lemma with base scheme $S=U$, quasi-coherent module $F$, and arbitrary $v:V\to U$ in $\mathcal B$. It gives $\check H^p(\mathcal V,G)=0$ for every $\mathcal V\in\mathrm{Cov}$ and $p>0$, with exactly the tensor-pullback restrictions used here. Its hypotheses require affineness only for $V$ and its covering members, and impose no flatness or finiteness condition on $F$. This verifies hypothesis (3).

source.place: Tag 03FJ, lemma-standard-covering-Cech-quasi-coherent; used in Tag 03DW proof, first affine-objects paragraph.

proof.text: The general-site Cech criterion now gives $H^q(V,G)=0$ for all $V\in\mathcal B$ and $q>0$. Take the terminal object $\operatorname{id}_U$, which belongs to $\mathcal B$ because $U$ is affine. Cohomology over this object is the right derived functor of its evaluation in abelian sheaves, hence is exactly $H^q(\mathcal C_U,(F^a)_{ab})$ in the question. This proves the asserted vanishing.
